description: The true path of The Same Monday told from its data (the same moves): two days. On the first the office, the pilot and the chandler's; the day ends, and on the second the inn and the watchman. What was learned on the first day is kept.

moves.why: The office first: how was it got into?
Locked, and never forced: whoever took the chart had a key.
Two keys and no more: the Captain's and the pilot's.
The pilot carries the other key: I will ask him about it.
He says he lent it to Finch at four and was without it all night. That is his word only.
Then Finch must say where he was.
The three hours are spent, and it is one man's word against another's. The same Monday again: this time the inn.
The coach stops at the Ship: Mrs. Pask will know when the Captain left.
The Captain and his key were at Marlow all night.
He could not have been in the office.
And the watchman was on the quay that night.
A key with a brass tally: the pilot's key carries one. It was the second key that Finch had.
So Finch had the pilot's key by the office that night: the pilot told the truth.
The pilot had no key that night.
The one key that was in Saltby that night was in Finch's hand, at the office door.
And he was not in his bed: the watchman met him on the quay.
